catalog_quote: 17. STRESS. As a rule, a stem in Mori (a fortiori a word) consists of two or more syllables. ... one-syllable words are in Mori, just as in Pamona, always proclitics or enclitics. They thus cannot occur independently nor carry their own stress. Only words of two or more syllables, then, qualify for stress placement. ... Stress in Mori is placed on the penultimate syllable, so that the language is missing an important tool for keeping oneself aware of the derivation of words formed with suffixes. For stress placement the same applies of enclitics, so that one says for example ambáu 'carabao', but with the emphatic particle mo: ambaúmo 'a cárabao'; likewise mateómo 'he is already dead' ... raháno 'his house', opuáno 'its stem', inia mámi 'our village', etc. etc. If there are four syllables, in general the initial syllable receives secondary stress. sources.citation: Barsel, Linda A. 1994. The verb morphology of Mori, Sulawesi. Pacific Linguistics B-111. Canberra: Australian National University. x+139 pp. (online ed. CC BY-SA, sealang/CRCL)
sources.quote: 'There are two kinds of stress in Mori, primary and secondary, both of which are predictable and distinguished by loudness and pitch. ... Primary stress falls on the penultimate syllable of any simple phrase' (me'ene / mee'neno; 'siru / si'rumu; lu'mako / lumako 'aku — enclitics/suffixes shift stress). 'There are three exceptions to this rule. The first two exceptions are the monosyllabic particles ke ... and ma ... These particles always receive primary stress. The third exception is the sequence ...(C)V(+)V+CV#, which optionally receives primary stress on the third syllable to the left of th
sources.locator: Ch. 2 (phonology of the Mokole dialect), sec. 2.2 p.~19 (long vowels and stress) and sec. 2.3 'Stress', 2.3.1-2.3.2, pp. 25-27
sources.note: Only post-Esser first-hand description of the same dialect (Mokole = Mori Bawah) with an explicit stress section (2.3, pp. 25-27); confirms penultimate primary stress with clitic shift, ke/ma exceptions and VV = two syllables, and gives a morpheme-based secondary-stress rule plus an optional antepenultimate variant for...V+V+CV# that could be added to the record's srule/exceptions.
